guide.h2: What a handyman should not do
p: Any work on gas, including moving a gas pipe or fitting a hob, must be done by a Gas Safe registered engineer. Larger electrical work, such as new circuits or a consumer unit, should be done by a registered electrician so you get the right certificates. See our lists of plumbers in Leeds and electricians in Leeds.

guide.h2: Getting the most from a handyman
p: Most handymen charge by the hour, half day or day. Write a list of every small job, with photos, and send it before the visit. Buy any materials you have chosen yourself, or agree that the handyman will supply them at cost. Grouping jobs into one visit is usually much cheaper than several call outs.
For a bigger single job, such as a new door lock, a full room of plastering or a fence, a specialist may do it faster and better. See locksmiths in Leeds for locks, or our full list of Leeds trades.

faqs.q: How much does a handyman charge in Leeds?
faqs.a: Most charge by the hour or by the half day. Ask for the rate and any minimum charge when you book. Our handyman cost guide is coming in a later update.

faqs.q: Can a handyman do electrical work?
faqs.a: Small like for like jobs, such as replacing a light fitting, may be fine, but new circuits and consumer units should be done by a registered electrician who can certify the work.

faqs.q: Will a handyman take a small job?
faqs.a: Many will, especially if you can add a few more jobs to make it worth the visit. Ask about a minimum charge.

faqs.q: Do handymen bring their own tools and materials?
faqs.a: They bring tools. Materials are usually extra, either bought by you or supplied by the handyman and added to the bill.
